transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: Tue May 12 2026, 3:00 PM PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Elena (CSM), Aiden, Priya, Diego, Sofia (Latitudeforge)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on pilot scope, runtime options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), networking needs, security checklist (SOC2, KMS), and logistics for a baseline benchmark. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
1) Pilot success criteria and timeline
2) Network and security constraints for private deployment
3) Baseline perf targets and cost expectations
4) Observability and escalation for go/no-go

Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining uh we'll do a quick roll call and then jump into goals, um Connor and Elena from our side.
[00:12] Aiden: hey thanks, Aiden here (Head of ML) excited to get started.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, platform eng. we'll own the infra side and network.
[00:20] Diego: Diego, InfoSec. I'll be asking the compliance bits.
[00:23] Sofia: Sofia, product. I want to understand latencies and cost tradeoffs.
[00:27] Maya: Awesome, quick agenda: map success criteria, decide pilot topology, share required artifacts and timeline. Sound good?
[00:31] All: yep / sounds good.
[00:34] Connor: i'll start with a short overview of where teams typically pilot with Redwood: most customers start hosted for speed, then either move to Dedicated reserved GPU pools or Private VPC when they need network isolation or specific KMS. There's a middle path where you can do hosted but pin models and use our prefix caching to control unit cost.
[00:55] Sofia: can you define Dedicated vs Private again — is Dedicated multitenant infra or single-tenant?
[01:02] Connor: good question; Dedicated is a reserved pool for a single customer — the GPUs are reserved and we guarantee throughput targets, but networking still goes over our managed network. Private gives you a customer-controlled VPC and optionally an on-prem package.
[01:18] Priya: if we need VPC peering and strict egress controls, is Private the only option?
[01:23] Elena: Private VPC yes, we can arrange peering, we also support customer-managed proxies. One thing to note, private/on-prem has a slightly longer onboarding (infra handshake and cert exchange).
[01:36] Diego: SOC2 and audit logs — do you provide full request-level audit logs and retention options? we need 12 months by default and 7 years for certain records.
[01:44] Maya: we provide request and token-level traces, plus configurable retention. For enterprise Private we can pipeline logs to customer S3 or SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 + logging export doc after this call.
[01:53] Diego: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (HSM)?
[01:57] Connor: yes, KM integration is supported for Private, and for Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key options using standard KMS integrations. On hosted there's a managed key setup but we can discuss contractual requirements for BYOK.
[02:10] Aiden: on performance, our main KPI is 95th percentile < 220ms for short completions (~32 tokens) and cost per 1k tokens needs to be under our internal threshold. Is that realistic?
[02:21] Connor: 220ms p95 is ambitious on hosted depending on model size — for smaller quantized models we hit low latencies, larger models will be higher. There are levers: batching vs continous batching, KV prefix cache, and model variant routing to a cheaper fall back. We should baseline with your real prompt distribution.
[02:40] Sofia: what's continuous batching? i've seen that term in your docs.
[02:43] Connor: it's our runtime feature to aggregate concurrent requests into micro-batches without adding head-of-line latency for single requests. helps throughput and cost when you have mixed QPS. The tradeoff is some variability in tail latencies, which we tune per-route.
[02:58] Priya: for the pilot, we want deterministic networking and stable SLA. timeline-wise can we go from kickoff to a 2-week pilot in 2-3 weeks?
[03:07] Elena: yes that's typical if we do hosted or dedicated; Private will add scheduling for infra handoff — usually add 1-2 weeks.
[03:15] Priya: we have strict egress proxies and an internal cert process, may take a few days.
[03:20] Diego: on the legal side, we might need a DPA + data processing annex, any standard forms?
[03:24] Maya: we have standard DPA templates; I'll include a copy. For unusual residency or deletion needs we'll surface it to legal.
[03:31] Aiden: about benchmarking — we want to run batch of synthetic and then our real traffic for 1 hour to measure p50/p95 and token costs. what's Redwood's suggested runbook?
[03:40] Connor: we recommend: 1) sample 1k prompts representative of checks, 2) run an unloaded baseline then a loaded 1-hour pass at target QPS, 3) capture latency, token counts, KV cache hit rates. We'll provide a template and a script to ingest into your infra or run from Redwood.
[03:59] Sofia: do you support streaming responses? some of our UX depends on partial token streaming.
[04:03] Connor: yes fully supported in hosted and dedicated. For Private it depends on the network path but generally yes. Streaming tends to increase the connection churn, but it's supported.
[04:14] Priya: about observability — we need per-route dashboards and trace links for SRE alerts. can we get Prometheus metrics or push to Datadog?
[04:22] Elena: we provide per-route telemetry and export hooks. Datadog integration and S3/CloudWatch exports are standard. We'll share dashboard templates.
[04:29] Diego: one more — does Redwood maintain a runbook for incident response and what access do you need for runbooks on our side?
[04:35] Maya: we have an incident playbook and a bridge process. For private installs we do a joint runbook review and limited cross-access for escalation, documented and auditable.
[04:44] Aiden: curious about model management: can we pin model versions and roll back if QA sees regressions?
[04:49] Connor: absolutely. You can pin a version, do canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies if latency or error thresholds breach. We also tie regressions to eval sets for automated alerts.
[04:59] Sofia: any gotchas for using quantized models for cost savings? we care about quality drop.
[05:04] Connor: quantization depends on model architecture; some open models keep quality with 8-bit or 4-bit quant. We'll recommend a quantization profile and run evals on your prompt set to measure quality delta. That's part of Redwood Optimize.
[05:18] Priya: on quotas and throttling — if we test a sudden spike can you scale fast enough?
[05:22] Elena: Dedicated is best for predictable spikes; hosted can burst but subject to region capacity. For the pilot we'll size for expected peak and add a buffer.
[05:33] Diego: security question: network egress — do you do packet inspection on your side? any PII controls pre-tokenization?
[05:41] Connor: we avoid inspecting payloads beyond necessary logs; for Private you can disable certain telemetry and route logs to your SIEM. For PII controls we recommend client-side obfuscation or tokenization before sending. We'll include recommended patterns.
[05:55] Maya: ok let's walk through a concrete pilot proposal. Connor?
[05:59] Connor: proposal outline: 2-week pilot, hosted with reserved Dedicated nodes as option. Stage 1: hosted quickstart (3 days) to validate prompts and metrics. Stage 2: benchmark run (1 day) then week-long stress run. If you need VPC, parallel infra readiness work starts and we aim to flip to Private in week 3.
[06:22] Priya: do you have a standard cost estimate for the pilot? rough ballpark to review now?
[06:26] Connor: rough rule: baseline for a modest pilot with small-medium model and moderate QPS — expect $Xk for the 2-week run including tokens and reserved compute. i'll send a detailed cost model — it's heavily dependent on model choice and QPS.
[06:38] Aiden: can you support our in-house fine-tuned variant? we use a small custom head on an open model.
[06:44] Connor: yes we can host fine-tuned weights; for Private there are fewer transfer constraints. For hosted we need to validate format and discuss model license.
[06:53] Sofia: about support SLAs — for pilot do we get 24/7 on-call?
[06:57] Elena: pilot includes business-hours coverage and priority slack channel; enterprise plans include 24/7 depending on contract.
[07:06] Diego: I'm concerned about latency if your routing falls back to another region during capacity constraints. do you do region pinning?
[07:13] Maya: yes requests can be pinned to region; we also have fallback policies but you can restrict fallbacks to avoid cross-region traffic.
[07:21] Priya: i will share our VPC and proxy constraints after this call, names and owners.
[07:26] Diego: also need to see encryption at rest and in transit specifics for the pilot.
[07:30] Maya: i'll attach the KMS and encryption doc.
[07:34] Sofia: any immediate blockers you see for us to start hosted pilot this week?
[07:39] Connor: only sample prompt set and API keys to run tests; Maya will send onboarding instructions and a small script.
[07:46] Aiden: timeline check — if we get script and keys today could we run a small smoke test by Friday?
[07:51] Maya: yes, assuming access approvals internally.
[07:55] Diego: legal will review the DPA, but we can do smoke test under NDA.
[07:59] Maya: good. quick note on telemetry: we'll provide a shared dashboard and a short training doc for your SREs.
[08:07] Priya: what's the typical token accounting cadence? day-by-day?
[08:11] Elena: we show per-minute and daily aggregations in the console and exportable CSVs.
[08:16] Sofia: any references from companies with similar constraints? would be helpful.
[08:20] Maya: we'll include references for companies in regulated spaces and a case study that emphasizes VPC/on-prem handoffs.
[08:27] Connor: last technical thing — if you want to run inference inside your network we support a private runtime package; it's a containerized bundle with a lightweight control plane. It needs a small footprint of GPUs and some cert exchange.
[08:42] Priya: that sounds promising. we'll review capacity and let you know.
[08:46] Aiden: for the benchmark, include KV cache hit metric. that's key for us.
[08:50] Connor: yep, we'll surface KV cache hit and prefix reuse stats.
[08:54] Maya: wrap-up: owners and due dates are in action items. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark window and share artifacts.
[09:03] Sofia: thanks everyone, this was efficient.
[09:06] Diego: thanks.
[09:08] Maya: end notes: attaching deck + onboarding playbook + security pack after call.
[09:12] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcribed words (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V cash" in auto transcript), speaker labels corrected post-hoc where possible but some segments may show generic speaker numbering in raw export.
